name: Tetraethylenepentamine
description: Tetraethylenepentamine (CAS 112-57-2 ), commonly known as TEPA or Tetren, is a polyamine used across coatings, polymer, and textile industries as a curing agent, crosslinker, and pH modifier. Its multiple reactive amine groups make it a functional building block for epoxy systems, chelating formulations, and specialty chemical synthesis. In epoxy coatings and adhesives, TEPA acts as a hardener. This material crosslinks resin networks to deliver durable, chemically resistant films suited for industrial and protective coating applications. Polymer manufacturers use it as a reactive intermediate. It is essential in producing polyamide resins and flame-retardant additives, where its nitrogen-rich structure contributes to char formation under heat exposure. In textile and paper processing, it functions well. TEPA serves as a wet-strength resin precursor and fiber treatment agent, improving substrate durability and dye uptake. Personal care formulators incorporate it at low concentrations for pH adjustment. This is particularly useful in rinse-off products where controlled alkalinity is required. TEPA is supplied as a viscous amber liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 95% to 98% depending on the supplier. Some producers offer blended or diluted formulations. These variations target specific epoxy curing or chelation applications.
